title: Session Hint Annotation Playbook
content:
Quick note / sandbox for session-hint annotations. Purpose: define a light-weight client->runtime hinting API that can be attached to session start and updated mid-session. Goal is to improve prefetching/pinning/kv-cache warmup while keeping surface area small and privacy-safe.

Status: rough draft. This is intentionally permissive (best-effort hints). Not an authz mechanism; hints can be ignored.

Motivation:
- Many clients can predict next-turn tokens or high-level intent (e.g., composing an email, code edit) and could give the runtime a short hint to prewarm model variants / KV keys.
- Want to avoid moving heavy logic to client; hints should be compact and interpretable by routing/prefetching components.
- Keep telemetry so we can measure signal quality and cost/benefit.

Principles:
- Hints are advisory only (non-binding).
- Size limit: 2KB per hint payload.
- No sensitive user data in hints (we need a guideline). If hint might include PII, require client-side flag `sensitive: true` (runtime should treat as non-cacheable).
- Hints attached to a session, and optionally to specific turns.

Core API shape (HTTP/JSON) - session-level:
POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/hints
Body: {
  "hint_id": "short-uuid",
  "source": "client-sdk|browser|mobile|plugin",
  "timestamp": "2025-02-10T15:22:13Z",
  "intent_tags": ["compose:email", "code:refactor"],
  "prefetch_profile": "fast|balanced|thorough",
  "kv_keys": ["user:recent_docs:prefix=invoice"],
  "sensitive": false,
  "weight": 0.7,  // 0..1 confidence score (optional)
  "expires_in": 60 // seconds of relevance
}
Response: 202 Accepted + {"applied": true|false, "reasons": [...]} 

Turn-level update (attach to an incoming request):
POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/turns/{turn_id}/hints
Body similar but narrower fields allowed (intent_tags, short text anchor, small token sample)

Examples of allowed kv_keys:
- "doc:1234:prefix=conclusion"
- "kb:policy:recent"
Guideline: keys should be opaque namespace tokens that the runtime can map to cached prefixes. Client should not invent global keys unless integrated with product team.

Routing/behaviour heuristics (runtime sketch):
1) Validate hint schema. Reject if >2KB or missing required fields.
2) If sensitive==true -> do not persist to shared cache, only ephemeral prefetch for this session.
3) Weight threshold: if weight >= 0.6 and prefetch_profile != 'none', run prefetch pipeline.
4) Prefetch_profile mapping:
   - fast -> minimal warmup (KV fetch + small context token prewarm)
   - balanced -> KV fetch + medium sequence prefix + model variant warmup
   - thorough -> full context prefetch and spin up an extra replica if allowed by quota
5) Rate-limit per-session hints: max 10 per minute; global per-tenant soft cap configurable.
6) Metrics emitted: hint.received, hint.prefetch.started, hint.prefetch.completed, hint.prefetch.skipped(reason), hint.hit_within_30s.

Telemetry event schema (flat map for now):
{
  "event": "hint.prefetch.completed",
  "session_id": "s-abc123",
  "hint_id": "h-xy9",
  "profile": "balanced",
  "duration_ms": 120,
  "kb_hits": 3,
  "cost_tokens_prefetched": 480,
  "applied": true
}
Note: we should keep telemetry names consistent with existing observability prefixes (per-route/model dashboards).

Cost modelling and safety:
- Prefetching costs tokens (if we generate continuations) or compute (KV fetch). Need to attribute to the session owner and surface in per-route cost breakdown.
- Suggest adding a duck-typed field `prefetch_budget_tokens` on session config to limit token spend. If a tenant has no budget, runtime should only do KV prefetch, not token generation.

Edge cases / attack vectors:
- Malicious clients sending many hints to inflate token usage. -> enforce per-API-key rate limits + exponential backoff.
- Cross-tenant leakage: hints referencing shared KV keys could poison caching. -> default: hints are local-tenant-scoped, and runtime only accepts kv_keys from a allowlist or mapped namespace.
- Sensitive content: if clients accidentally include PII, mark `sensitive: true` required by SDK; runtime must honor and avoid shared caches.

Lifecycle operations / admin controls:
- Console toggle per-tenant: Hints enabled | heuristics only | disabled.
- Rollout plan: start with internal beta tenants, then opt-in alpha, collect hit rates and cost delta, then widen.
- Audit log: every prefetch action must record hint_id, session, and decision reason.

Sample client flow (ASCII diagram):
Client (SDK) -> session.start (with hint payload) -> Ingress -> Hint validator -> Prefetch controller -> (KV store) / (Model warmup) -> Runtime cache

Sketch of decision function pseudo: 
function shouldPrefetch(hint, sessionConfig, tenantConfig) {
  if (tenantConfig.hintsEnabled == false) return false;
  if (hint.sensitive) return sessionConfig.allowSensitivePrefetch;
  if (hint.weight && hint.weight < sessionConfig.minPrefetchConfidence) return false;
  if (sessionConfig.remainingPrefetchBudgetTokens <= 0) return false;
  return true;
}

SDK ergonomics notes:
- Provide a small helper in JS/Swift/Kotlin that builds hints from higher-level client signals (e.g., UI intent tags, selected text).
- Auto-sanitizer that flags long free-text anchor fields as sensitive by default.
- Backpressure callback when server returns applied:false with reason=quota -> show spinner/disable prefetch UI.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Exact schema for kv_keys: free-form strings vs structured (namespace:key:attrs). Prefer structured but need mapping plan.
- Telemetry retention and sampling: we should sample heavy prefetch events to avoid SSO blowup.
- UX for product teams to register allowed key namespaces (Console UI design).
- Should hints be signed by the SDK to prevent spoofing? How much value does that add vs rate limits + API keys?
- Interop with Dedicated / Private deployments: for on-prem, policy for cross-tenant caches is different. Document separately.

Experimentation checklist (quick):
- [ ] Implement validator + simple prefetch controller in dev cluster (A)
- [ ] Add telemetry counters to console dashboard (B)
- [ ] Ship SDK helper for JS (C)
- [ ] Run small alpha with 3 tenants for 2 weeks, measure hit_within_30s and cost delta
- [ ] Iterate on schema (kv_keys structured vs free)

Notes to self / TODO for doc polishing:
- Move pseudocode to runtime repo as a WORKING-LIBRARY example.
- Add sample curl examples showing accepted / rejected hints.
- Align metric names with product observability team.

Rough sample cURL: 
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/sessions/s-123/hints" -H "Authorization: Bearer token" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "hint_id": "h-456",
  "source": "browser",
  "intent_tags": ["compose:email"],
  "prefetch_profile": "fast",
  "kv_keys": ["user:recent_docs:prefix=inbox"],
  "weight": 0.8,
  "expires_in": 45
}'

Appendix: minimal JSON schema (draft):
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "title": "session-hint",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["hint_id","source","timestamp"],
  "properties": {
    "hint_id": {"type":"string"},
    "source": {"type":"string"},
    "timestamp": {"type":"string","format":"date-time"},
    "intent_tags": {"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},
    "prefetch_profile": {"type":"string","enum":["none","fast","balanced","thorough"]},
    "kv_keys": {"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},
    "sensitive": {"type":"boolean"},
    "weight": {"type":"number","minimum":0,"maximum":1},
    "expires_in": {"type":"integer","minimum":1}
  }
}

End of playbook (for now). Keep this as the working notes for the feature spike.

References / links I pasted above: Linear PH-412, runtime PR 987. Slack thread: #prefetch-playbook (internal).

-- Maya
